new_statements.quote: Ikpeshi is a Proto-North West Edoid language, it is one of the languages used in Edo State, South-South Nigeria. It has a similar linguistic features with Edo (Bini). This study is an investigation into the phonology of Ikpeshi language with the view to determine the sound system of the language, phonological processes like vowel elision, vowel assimilation glide formation, nasalization; syllable and tonal patterns operational the language. The methodology employed in this work is descriptive. The theoretical framework was Goldsmith Autosegmental theory.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid ikpe1243 (HTML + JSON) and reference 550315; Wikipedia 'Ikpeshi language' and 'Edoid languages' wikitext; Wikidata Q3912777; Ethnologue 22 (2019) 'Ikpeshi' via the Internet Archive; ASJP wordlist IKPESHI (from Bradbury 1968).
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog: zero descriptive refs; Glottolog's most extensive description = Bradbury 1968 comparative Edo wordlists (a wordlist or less); page lists Lewis 2013 and Ethnologue 2025 only. Ethnologue 2019: alternate names Ekpeshe, Ikpeshe; North-Central > Ghotuo-Uneme-Yekhee; no language resources. Wikipedia cites only Lewis 2015 (USEM), Agheyisi 1984 (word, minority-language list) and Ekwukoma & Odiagbe 2025. ASJP holds a Bradbury-1968-based wordlist, no prosody.

sources.note: Ethnographic survey (source of the 1,826 population figure cited by Blench/Wikipedia). The archive.org scan has no text; a 200-dpi scanned of the index region (pp.196-215) is too poor to use and shows no 'Ikpeshi'. Not a linguistic description; not read further.

sources.note: Nothing. Lexical diffusion study built on 500-item wordlists elicited in 36 villages; Ikpeshi appears only as a member of lexical sets (items (1) sleep, (14)-(18), (24) person, (26) see/big/old) and in sec. 9 'Orle Diffusion Belt' ('the valley settlements of Okpella, North Ibie, Atte, Ikpeshi, Ososo.. have exclusive vocabulary stemming from diffusion', p.138). sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Nothing on Ikpeshi phonology. Ikpeshi is a 'one-village community' (p.68); on mutual intelligibility it belongs to the Akoko-Edo group 'Atte Ikpeshi-Enwan-Okpilla-North Ibie (NWE)' (p.68); the Northern Edo project recorded narrative tapes at Ikpeshi, which 'have been transcribed and translated', and collected an Ibadan-400 wordlist for all NE communities (pp.71-72) -- all unpublished. Table 8 on NCE/NWE tone systems has no Ikpeshi row; stress is not mentioned.
